input.quote: b. paying the applicable early termination charges, if any, specified in Attachment A and applicable Service Option Attachments.
input.rationale: Section 3.4(b) makes Customer's convenience termination conditional on paying uncapped "early termination charges" set in Attachment A and Service Option Attachments (documents not in these Base Terms), and nothing states that this is the only liquidated amount Customer can owe on termination. That is a Customer-payable liquidated amount with no ceiling, so it fails the fallback (three months' fees, sole liquidated amount). We target the fallback rather than deleting 3.4(b), because Section 3.3 expressly cross-refers to "the early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b)" and deletion would leave a dangling reference. Late payment fees in 4.2 and the Section 9.2 liability cap are not liquidated damages and are not flagged.

ops.text: The early termination charges described in Section 3.4(b) will not exceed three (3) months' charges and are the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer under this Agreement.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we pay no liquidated damages or penalties; where an early-termination charge is unavoidable, we cap it at three months' charges and make it the only liquidated amount payable by us. We have added this as a separate sentence so Section 3.4(b) and the cross-reference in Section 3.3 remain intact.
proposal.summary: Cap the early termination charge at three months' charges and make it the sole Customer-payable liquidated amount.

mappings.element: Any Customer-payable liquidated amount is only an early-termination fee.
The early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
The early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
